Revenue from electricity sales is generally recognized as the units are produced and delivered within the production month. Capacity charges, representing the reservation of an electric generating facility, are recognized as a single performance obligation transferred over time, typically on a monthly basis. For wholesale customers, the transaction price is determined using rates, charges, terms, and conditions of service approved by the FERC. These rates include both fixed (base rate) and variable (formula-based) components. The base rate is often set using a formula derived from the prior year’s expenses, while the variable component is trued up to reflect actual current-year costs. This means that variable consideration is estimated and recognized over time as services are provided. When the actual costs differ from those estimated and billed, a true-up adjustment is made, which may result in additional revenue recognized or refunded to customers. In summary, WEC Energy Group recognizes revenue for fixed charges as the service is provided (over time), and for variable charges, revenue is estimated and adjusted based on actual costs through a true-up process, recognizing revenue as the customer receives and consumes the services.
